question: Should ClawSweeper adopt an opt-in policy that reduces broad review capacity when the exact-review queue is saturated, and if so, what thresholds and rollback conditions govern the trial?
rationale: Tests can verify the implementation mechanics, but only maintainers can choose whether cross-workflow background throttling matches operational priorities and define acceptable backlog, latency, and starvation tradeoffs.

options.title: Sponsor a staged trial
options.body: Land telemetry first, narrow this branch to scheduler policy, and run a default-off trial with explicit 16/4 threshold justification, success metrics, and rollback conditions.

options.title: Keep telemetry only
options.body: Proceed with https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/555 and close the scheduler experiment unless later production evidence demonstrates a need for adaptive yielding.

options.title: Defer the experiment
options.body: Leave this PR draft until a future backlog event provides a controlled test window and an agreed operational owner.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged trial
recommendation.body: Land telemetry first, narrow this branch to scheduler policy, and run a default-off trial with explicit 16/4 threshold justification, success metrics, and rollback conditions.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged exact-review incident recovery and are best positioned to judge whether an additional scheduling policy is operationally warranted.
